Introduction
This document provides essential information on the components of the Opportunities in Green Building
Key Issue to enable users of ESG Ratings to understand how MSCI Sustainability & Climate’s (MSCI
S&C’s), outputs are determined. Opportunities in Green Building is a Key Issue in the Environmental Pillar
of the MSCI ESG Ratings model. Companies are evaluated based on the resource consumption and
carbon intensity of their property assets, their potential exposure to environmental building regulations
and their efforts to improve the environmental performance of their real estate assets.
For additional details on the MSCI ESG Ratings Model, refer to the Data, ratings and scores section of
“ESG Ratings Methodology.”

The definitions of the data points in each component are given below:
Opportunities in Green Building Practices score
The Opportunities in Green Building Practices score evaluates the company’s ability to manage its
exposure to opportunities related to the resource consumption and carbon intensity of its property
assets and its efforts to improve the environmental performance of its real estate assets. This score is a
component of the Opportunities in Green Building Management score and considers attributes of the
company's policies and initiatives. It is expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates strong initiatives.
• Extent of green building certification commitments in portfolio or development pipeline
Definition: The portion of the company’s portfolio or development projects that are covered by its green
building commitments. Applies to real estate companies only.

• Extent of commercial arrangements to improve or maintain property environmental
performance
Definition: Indicates whether the company provides evidence of implementing commercial agreements
to incentivize tenants and property managers to improve property environmental performance. Applies
to real estate companies only.
• Use of green or triple-net leases
Definition: Indicates whether the company provides evidence of implementing green leases or triple-net
leases in its tenancies. Applies to real estate companies only.
• Green certification commitments related to greenfield developments
Definition: The company’s green building strategy for greenfield sites, including whether there is a clear
statement on avoiding greenfield sites, the company only develops green-certified properties on
greenfield developments, or we found no evidence of green certification for greenfield developments.
Applies to real estate companies only.
• Evidence of flexible or mixed-use properties in portfolio
Definition: Indicates whether the company provides evidence of flexible or mixed-use properties in its
property portfolio. Applies to real estate companies only.
• Evidence of urban revitalization developments
Definition: The level of urban redevelopment that the company undertakes. Best practice is urban
revitalization. Applies to real estate companies only.
• Green building commitment extends to existing buildings in portfolio (in addition to new
buildings)
Definition: Indicates whether the company renovates or redevelops its existing properties with either
green building initiatives or green building certifications. Applies to real estate companies only.

Opportunities in Green Building Performance score
The Opportunities in Green Building Performance score evaluates the company’s performance on
opportunities in green building metrics (including percentage of green-certified buildings and space, and
carbon emissions ) relative to its peers. It is expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest
level of performance.
The following provides a non-exhaustive overview of the indicators and sub-indicators used in the
assessment of the Opportunities in Green Building Performance score.
• Green building certification score
Definition: Assesses the extent of certified spaces or buildings under selected green building
standards. Expressed as a 0-10 score, with 10 indicating highest level of certification coverage
across the portfolio.
o Score of green certified buildings as % of total
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the share of green-certified
buildings within its real estate portfolio, calculated as the percentage of total buildings
that hold recognized green building certifications. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10
indicates the highest level of performance.
o Score of green certified space as % of total
Definition: Assesses the company’s performance on the share of green-certified space
within its real estate portfolio, calculated as the percentage of total floor area that holds
recognized green building certifications. Expressed as a 0–10 score, where 10 indicates
the highest level of performance.
o Evidence of green certified buildings in real estate portfolio
Definition: Assesses the extent to which the company provides verifiable evidence of
green-certified buildings within its real estate portfolio, based on the availability and
quality of supporting documentation such as certification records or third-party registries.
Expressed as a 0–5 score, where 10 indicates comprehensive and verifiable evidence.
• Carbon emissions performance relative to peers
Definition: Assesses the company's performance on greenhouse gas [GHG] emissions intensity
(normalized by sales or by units of production), and trend in GHG emissions intensity, relative to
its peers. Expressed as a 0-10 score, where 10 indicates the highest level of performance.

The Energy Certification score for a given business activity is based on the proportion of total building
area that is certified to the ENERGY STAR certification for buildings.
The Energy Use Intensity score is based on the aggregate energy use intensity for each business activity
in thousands of British thermal units per square foot.
The Water Use Intensity score is based on the volume of water used for each business activity in gallons
per square foot. A score of 10 indicates the highest opportunity.

The near-term ambition of a country is assessed by considering the annual emissions reduction rate
needed to meet their publicly disclosed near-term climate targets. Countries with aggressive near-term
targets have high emissions reduction rates and therefore a higher policy pressure segment score.
A country or market’s long-term ambition indicates the strength and credibility of its long-term climate
targets such as net-zero commitments. Long term targets could signal the direction of future policy and
regulatory developments, even in the near term.
The government and market mechanisms score indicates the current strength of policy and market-
based mechanisms signaling a government’s commitment to driving the energy transition.
This score is calculated as the average of carbon pricing score and fossil fuel subsidies score.

systems that exert policy pressure on companies by assigning a direct cost to carbon emissions.
The fossil fuel subsidies score indicates the degree of financial support for fossil fuel consumption.
Lower subsidies (higher scores) increase transition pressure by removing cost advantages, whereas high
subsidies (lower scores) signal continued alignment with fossil fuel-based economic structures, thus

In the absence of evidence from data sources indicating that a country has near- or long-term emissions
reduction targets or carbon pricing mechanisms in place, a score of 0 is assigned. In the absence of a
country’s fossil fuel subsidy information, a score of 5 is assigned.
